question.text: Saraswati Growth Fund is being set up as a Category II AIF with a proposed corpus of INR 400 crore. Compute the minimum continuing interest that the Sponsor/Manager must contribute into the scheme as per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012.

answer.text: INR 5 crore (lower of 2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Regulation 10(d) of SEBI (AIF) Regulations mandates Sponsor/Manager continuing interest of the LOWER of 2.5% of corpus OR INR 5 crore for Category I/II AIFs. Here, 2.5% of INR 400 crore = INR 10 crore; but the cap is INR 5 crore, so the lower figure INR 5 crore applies. Skin-in-the-game cannot be through waiver of management fees. **The Trap:** Option A picks the straight 2.5% figure, ignoring the INR 5 crore cap. Option C invokes the 1% figure that applies to Cat III (not Cat I/II) — regulatory fact trap. Option D is a fabricated floor. Candidates often miss 'lower of' language and compute only the 2.5%. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) asks the same number as a product feature. XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) tests the Cat III version (5% or INR 10 cr). XXI-B portfolio-manager skin-in-the-game rules (minimum INR 5 cr own funds) are separate — do not conflate with AIF Sponsor commit. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** At IC level, if the fund is large (say INR 1,000 cr), the INR 5 cr cap is trivial relative to fund economics but keeps founders aligned. Senior LPs routinely negotiate a 'GP commit above-the-minimum' side-letter covenant pushing Sponsor skin to 2-3% of total corpus as an alignment signal — disclose this in PPM.
